speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your symptoms of fatigue and itching, do you notice any yellowing of your skin or eyes, and have you experienced any changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Have you noticed any darkening of your urine or lightening of your stool, and do you have any history of alcohol use or recent medication changes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: You have scleral icterus, which confirms jaundice, and given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to rule out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. I will request an MRCP and further liver enzymes to investigate bile duct obstruction or inflammation. REQUEST TEST: MRCP, REQUEST TEST: ALP, GGT, IgG4

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRCP, ALP, GGT, IgG4: NORMAL READINGS

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP and IgG4 are normal, Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis and IgG4-related disease are less likely, so I need to investigate other causes of cholestasis and liver injury. Do you have any right upper quadrant abdominal pain, nausea, or a history of autoimmune conditions such as thyroid disease or rheumatoid arthritis?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal MRCP makes Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis unlikely, so I need to consider autoimmune hepatitis or other causes of cholestatic liver injury. Do you have any other autoimmune conditions like thyroid disease or rheumatoid arthritis, and have you started any new medications or supplements recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, diarrhea, joint pain, or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRCP and lack of extrahepatic causes, I am concerned about Autoimmune Hepatitis or Primary Biliary Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies, REQUEST TEST: Anti-nuclear antibodies, REQUEST TEST: Liver biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Anti-mitochondrial antibodies: Negative, Anti-nuclear antibodies: Negative, Liver biopsy: Not performed/Normal readings

speaker: Doctor
text: With autoimmune markers negative and PSC ruled out, your history of inconsistent condom use raises suspicion for viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis B surface antigen, REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis C antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Hepatitis B and C are negative, and given your history of ulcerative colitis, I must consider drug-induced liver injury or other metabolic causes. REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen level, REQUEST TEST: Ceruloplasmin, REQUEST TEST: Iron studies

speaker: Doctor
text: With toxic, metabolic, and common viral causes ruled out, I suspect an acute viral hepatitis from another source or atypical presentation. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A IgM, REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis E IgM

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hepatitis A IgM: Negative, Hepatitis E IgM: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient is a 32-year-old male with ulcerative colitis presenting with fatigue, pruritus, and jaundice. Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) is the most likely diagnosis given the strong association with ulcerative colitis, even though the initial MRCP was reported as normal (early PSC can have subtle or normal MRCP findings, and cholangiography is often required for definitive diagnosis). Autoimmune hepatitis, viral hepatitis, and metabolic causes have been ruled out by negative serologies and normal tests.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
